newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Brisbane airport buyers to spend A$300 mln over 10 years. [CORRECTED 08:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Brisbane airport buyers to spend A$300 mln over 10 years. [CORRECTED 08:55 GMT]

text.p: The winning bidder for Brisbane's international airport said on Wednesday it planned to spend A$300 million over 10 years as part of an ambitious expansion programme for the airport (Corrects from A$300 mln per year).

However, the Brisbane Airport Corporation Ltd (BACL) consortium, headed by the Dutch government-owned Amsterdam Airport Schipol and the Commonwealth Bank of Australia, had no immediate plans for an early stockmarket float, BACL director Koen Rooijmans told a news conference on Wednesday.
Earlier, the Federal government had announced the consortium had been awarded the airport ownership for a purchase price of A$1.387 billion.
Funding for the purchase would be a mixture of debt and equity, arranged by Commonwealth Bank with independent advice from Hambros Corporate Finance, BACL director Irene Lee said.
Consortium member, Brisbane City Council would contribute A$10 million of the purchase price and have one board seat on a nine-member board, councillor Tim Quinn said.
Rooijmans said the consortium had a 30-year development master plan for the airport with a second runway for the airport expected by about the year 2005.
